\begin{theorem}[Bounded Walk Loop Invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_loop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_loop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_K, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_cur, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_g, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_stp, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wb, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wt, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rK, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rcur, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rg, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.toV_wB, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.toV_wT, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwX, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₃_neg, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₃_pos, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_guess, Complexity.WalkLe}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be a relation on natural numbers, and let $b$ be a
Boolean value. Let $Q$ be a proposition and let $\sigma$ be a state whose registers are
all at most $B$. Write $w_b=\sigma.u$ and $q_b=\sigma.i$ when $b$ is true, and
$w_b=\sigma.v$ and $q_b=\sigma.i1$ otherwise. Suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$,
$\sigma.cur<\sigma.K$, and $\sigma.stp\le q_b$. If, whenever there is a walk from
$\sigma.cur$ to $w_b$ of at most $q_b-\sigma.stp$ steps, with each intermediate vertex
less than $\sigma.K$ and each step in $R$, the machine started at its walk-entry state
with $cur=stp=g=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$
holds, then the machine started at its walk-loop state with register values $\sigma$
terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when both such a walk exists and $Q$
holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Walk Initialization Correctness]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_spec}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_K, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.toV_g, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wb, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wt, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rK, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rcur, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwX, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_loop, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₂_neg, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₂_pos, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_guess, Complexity.WalkLe}
\difficulty{5}
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle on four indices and finite
Boolean words, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $Q$
be a proposition. Let $\sigma$ be a state whose registers are all at most $B$, and
suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$. Write $w_b=\sigma.u$ and $t_b=\sigma.i$ when $b$ is true, and
$w_b=\sigma.v$ and $t_b=\sigma.i1$ otherwise. If membership of $t_b$ in the set of codes
reachable from some initial code $u<\sigma.K$ by a walk of at most $\sigma.K$ steps
implies that the machine started at its walk-entry state with $cur=stp=g=0$ terminates
within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine started
at its walk-initialization state with register values $\sigma$ terminates within that
bound and accepts exactly when $t_b$ is so reachable and $Q$ holds. Here initial codes
and steps are determined by the oracle's initial-code and transition queries,
respectively, and each intermediate code in the walk is less than $\sigma.K$.
\end{theorem}
